title: Microsoft Purview: network DLP policies for all websites through Entra Internet Access
summary: The briefing passes: its roadmap targets, control paths, command and licensing requirements are supported. The unpublished all-websites scope is distinguished from today's documented integration. A broader Microsoft licensing page gives conflicting pay-as-you-go guidance that should also be acknowledged.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans all-websites network DLP scope through Entra GSA Internet Access.
claims.quote: admins can scope their network data security data loss prevention policies, integrated with Entra GSA Internet Access, to apply to all websites

claims.claim: The planned all-websites scope can exclude specific cloud apps.
claims.quote: all websites except specific cloud apps, allowing them to apply protection to cloud apps and websites that are not in the Defender Cloud App Catalog.

claims.claim: The roadmap status is In development.
claims.quote: "status": "In development"

claims.where: front matter: targetDate; What's changing; Scope

claims.quote: "targetDate": "December CY2026"

claims.claim: The preview target is November CY2026.
claims.quote: "previewDate": "November CY2026"

claims.quote: "clouds": [ "Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant)" ]

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; Why it matters; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated the new scope's arrival default.
claims.quote: Searched: "Purview" "all websites" "default"; read roadmap record, dlp-network-data-security-learn, dlp-create-policy-ai-network-data-security and how-to-network-content-filtering. None states the new scope's arrival default or migration of existing policies.

claims.where: What's changing; controls[0].note; Governance guidance; Open questions
claims.claim: Learn does not yet document the all-websites scope option or its exception picker.
claims.quote: Searched: "Purview" "all websites"; Purview network data security Entra Internet Access all websites exceptions default scope licensing cloud apps PowerShell Graph content filtering API. Opened both Purview network articles and Entra content filtering; they show catalog apps and adaptive scopes.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment
claims.claim: Today's documented network DLP data sources are unmanaged catalog apps and adaptive app scopes.
claims.quote: Data sources - These are the locations that the endpoint device is communicating with. Unmanaged cloud apps ... Adaptive app scopes

claims.claim: The Defender for Cloud Apps catalog includes over 35,000 discoverable cloud apps.
claims.quote: Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps Cloud app catalog which includes over 35,000 discoverable cloud apps.

claims.claim: Adaptive app scopes include generative AI, cloud storage, collaboration, social network and webmail categories.
claims.quote: Adaptive app scopes - all apps in multiple categories including generative AI, cloud storage, collaboration, social network, and webmail.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Network DLP supports Audit only and Block, including through GSA.
claims.quote: Network data security supports Audit only and Block actions. ... Microsoft Entra Global Secure Access supports all supported activities and actions.

claims.claim: The printed Purview path reaches the adaptive app scope picker for a network DLP policy.
claims.quote: Select Data loss prevention > Policies > + Create policy. ... Select Inline web traffic. ... Select Custom from the Categories list and then select Custom policy from the Regulations list. ... Select + Add cloud apps. ... Select the Adaptive app scopes tab

claims.claim: No documented automation parameter was found for choosing the cloud app scope of a network DLP policy.
claims.quote: Searched: "network" "DlpCompliancePolicy" "cloud apps" parameter; "network" "Set-DlpCompliancePolicy" "Locations". Read New-DlpCompliancePolicy Locations and ThirdPartyAppDlpLocation descriptions and Set excerpts; none identifies a network cloud-app picker parameter.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Governance controls table; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The printed Purview path reaches Network and non-Microsoft secure browsers on Choose where to enforce the policy.
claims.quote: Select Data loss prevention > Policies > + Create policy. ... Select Inline web traffic. ... Select Custom from the Categories list and then select Custom policy from the Regulations list. ... Choose where to enforce the policy ... Network and non-Microsoft secure browsers is On

claims.claim: New-DlpCompliancePolicy -EnforcementPlanes @("Network") creates a DLP policy with the Network enforcement plane.
claims.quote: The EnforcementPlanes parameter defines the layer where policy actions are run. ... -EnforcementPlanes @("<Value>"). Valid values are: ... Network

claims.claim: The New-DlpCompliancePolicy reference lists Network without a description of that value.
claims.quote: Application: For use with policies applied to Entra-registered enterprise applications in the organization. Application replaces the previous value Entra, which is now deprecated. - Network

claims.claim: New-DlpCompliancePolicy is available in Security & Compliance PowerShell and creates DLP policies.
claims.quote: This cmdlet is available only in Security & Compliance PowerShell. ... Use the New-DlpCompliancePolicy cmdlet to create data loss prevention (DLP) policies

claims.claim: The printed Entra path reaches the Scan with Purview action in a new content policy rule.
claims.quote: Browse to Global Secure Access > Secure > Content policies. ... Select + Create Policy. ... On the Basics tab ... On the Rules tab: Add a new rule. ... Select the appropriate option for the Action menu ... select Scan with Purview.

claims.claim: No documented API operation was found that sets a content rule's Scan with Purview action.
claims.quote: Searched: "networkAccess" "contentFiltering" "purview" action Graph; "contentFilteringRule" "purview"; "Scan with Purview" "graph" "action". Opened Entra content filtering and Graph beta filteringRule; no Scan with Purview property or action operation was documented.

claims.claim: The Entra content policy page provides portal steps rather than an automation call for Scan with Purview.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Entra admin center ... Browse to Global Secure Access > Secure > Content policies. ... To use data policies configured in Microsoft Purview, select Scan with Purview.

claims.claim: The documented GSA network data security entitlement is per-user/per-seat.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 E7 per-seat licenses ... Purview E5 (or equivalent) per-seat licenses and Entra Internet Access (or equivalent) licenses

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Governance guidance; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Microsoft 365 E7 per-seat licences are one entitlement route for network data security with GSA.
claims.quote: Network data security with Microsoft Entra Global Secure Access requires one of the following license combinations: Microsoft 365 E7 per-seat licenses

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Governance guidance; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The alternative entitlement is Purview E5 or equivalent per-seat licences plus Entra Internet Access or equivalent licences.
claims.quote: Purview E5 (or equivalent) per-seat licenses and Entra Internet Access (or equivalent) licenses

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Internet Access users also need Microsoft Entra ID P1 or P2.
claims.quote: To use Microsoft Entra Private Access and Microsoft Entra Internet Access, users need a Microsoft Entra ID P1 or Microsoft Entra ID P2 license.

claims.claim: The network data security overview says pay-as-you-go setup is not required for GSA integration.
claims.quote: Pay-as-you-go is not required to be set up for integration with Microsoft Entra Global Secure Access.
claims.fix: After this sentence add: 'The Microsoft Purview service description describes network DLP more generally as pay-as-you-go capabilities without stating this GSA exception; the network data security overview explicitly gives the exception.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/office365/servicedescriptions/microsoft-365-service-descriptions/microsoft-365-tenantlevel-services-licensing-guidance/microsoft-purview-service-description.

claims.claim: Non-Microsoft SASE and secure browser integrations require pay-as-you-go setup.
claims.quote: You must configure pay-as-you-go for your Microsoft 365 tenant to use Purview network data security with non-Microsoft SASE and secure browser solutions.

claims.claim: The content policy page requires valid Internet Access and Purview licences for Scan with Purview.
claims.quote: A valid Microsoft Entra Internet Access license. A valid Microsoft Purview license, required for Scan with Purview inspection.

claims.claim: The content policy page's portal-access note names Microsoft 365 E5/A5 or a Purview DLP add-on.
claims.quote: If you don't see Data loss prevention in Microsoft Purview ... You need a role such as DLP Compliance Management or Information Protection Admin, and a Microsoft 365 E5/A5 subscription or a Microsoft Purview DLP add-on.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: No price, meter, rate or licence rule specific to the new all-websites scope is published.
claims.quote: Searched: "Purview" "all websites" "price"; "Purview" "all websites" "scope" licensing default. Read network data security licensing/billing, GSA licensing overview, and Purview service description licensing search excerpts; none names a separate all-websites charge or entitlement.

claims.claim: The Entra page limits Scan with Purview file and text content to 3 MB.
claims.quote: The maximum supported content size for Scan with Purview is 3 MB for both file and text content types.

claims.claim: OCR is not yet supported for traffic sent to Purview.
claims.quote: OCR is not yet supported for traffic sent to Purview.

claims.claim: Scan with Purview only inspects traffic mapped to an Entra user identity.
claims.quote: Scan with Purview only applies to traffic associated with an Entra user identity. Traffic that cannot be mapped to an Entra user identity is not sent to Purview for inspection.

claims.claim: The Purview overview separately gives 4 MB limits for uploadText and downloadText.
claims.quote: Inline evaluation size limits: Microsoft Purview evaluates up to 4 MB of content for uploadText and downloadText

claims.claim: The Purview overview gives 3 MB limits for uploadFile and downloadFile.
claims.quote: files up to 3 MB for uploadFile and downloadFile.

claims.claim: Purview network data security policies do not apply to B2B guest users.
claims.quote: Purview network data security policies don't apply to B2B guest users.

claims.claim: The DLP walkthrough requires an Entra ID joined device for GSA.
claims.quote: If you're using Microsoft Entra Global Secure Access - The device must be Entra ID joined.

claims.claim: The Entra content policy page instead allows Entra ID joined or hybrid joined devices.
claims.quote: The Global Secure Access client requires a device (or virtual machine) that is either Microsoft Entra ID joined or Microsoft Entra ID Hybrid joined.

claims.claim: The GSA integration requires a TLS inspection policy.
claims.quote: You must configure a Transport Layer Security inspection policy

claims.claim: A GSA Internet Access content policy is required for the integration.
claims.quote: You must configure a content policy in Microsoft Entra GSA Internet Access.

claims.claim: Initial configuration requires enabling the Internet Access traffic forwarding profile.
claims.quote: Enable the Internet Access traffic forwarding profile and ensure correct user assignments.

claims.claim: The documented setup installs and configures the GSA client on Windows or macOS and routes internet traffic through GSA.
claims.quote: Install the Global Secure Access client on Windows or macOS. ... Before you continue, test and ensure your client's internet traffic is routed through Global Secure Access.

claims.where: controls[2].note; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: The content policy is configured by a Global Secure Access Administrator.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Entra admin center as a Global Secure Access Administrator.

claims.claim: DLP policy permissions include DLP Compliance Management or Information Protection Admin.
claims.quote: You need a role such as DLP Compliance Management or Information Protection Admin

claims.claim: The policy mode step offers simulation before enforcement.
claims.quote: On the Policy mode page, choose Turn the policy on immediately or run in simulation mode first to test.

claims.claim: Traffic is allowed fail-open when Purview inspection cannot complete.
claims.quote: In scenarios where Purview inspection is unable to complete, such as a payload that is too large to inspect, or an internal error, the traffic is allowed (fail-open).

claims.claim: Microsoft says to allow up to 24 hours for policy distribution and first data after integration configuration.
claims.quote: After you configure the integration between Microsoft Purview and your network security solution, allow up to 24 hours for your policies to be distributed to the network security solution and for the first data to show up.

claims.claim: Activity explorer can filter network policy events by the network enforcement plane.
claims.quote: In activity explorer, you can filter events with enforcement plane set to network. This filter shows you activities that network data security policies generate.

claims.claim: PurviewStatus in GSA traffic logs identifies transactions that skipped inspection.
claims.quote: Transactions that have skipped inspection can be identified in Traffic logs using PurviewStatus field.

claims.claim: The DLP walkthrough says some features used in its scenario are in preview.
claims.quote: Some features used in this scenario are in preview.

claims.claim: Scan with Purview requires a matching inline web traffic DLP policy.
claims.quote: If you choose the Scan with Purview action in a content policy rule, you must also configure a corresponding DLP policy in Microsoft Purview that targets inline web traffic.

claims.claim: Purview DLP rule actions should match the content policy's selected activities and content types.
claims.quote: The actions you select in the Purview DLP rule should match the content types and activities you selected in the Global Secure Access content policy.

claims.claim: Conditional Access policy configuration needs the Conditional Access Administrator role.
claims.quote: A Conditional Access Administrator role to configure Conditional Access policies.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Why it matters
claims.claim: The documented GSA licensing prerequisites concern the integration rather than a particular selected app scope.
claims.quote: A valid Microsoft Entra Internet Access license. A valid Microsoft Purview license, required for Scan with Purview inspection.

claims.claim: The roadmap says the new scope allows protection of apps and websites outside the Defender Cloud App Catalog.
claims.quote: allowing them to apply protection to cloud apps and websites that are not in the Defender Cloud App Catalog.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated whether existing policies change scope on arrival.
claims.quote: Searched: "Purview" "all websites" "default". Read roadmap record, Purview network data security overview and walkthrough, and Entra content filtering. None describes automatic migration or a scope change for existing policies.

claims.claim: The Entra content policy and the Purview DLP policy are separate objects.
claims.quote: If you selected the Scan with Purview action in your content policy, you must configure a corresponding data loss prevention (DLP) policy in Microsoft Purview.

claims.claim: Without a matching Purview DLP policy, the content policy cannot inspect selected content or enforce audit or block decisions.
claims.quote: Without a matching Purview DLP policy, the content policy can't inspect selected file or text content or enforce audit or block decisions.

claims.claim: The documented inspection limits apply to Scan with Purview itself rather than being exceptions for particular selected app scopes.
claims.quote: The maximum supported content size for Scan with Purview is 3 MB for both file and text content types. OCR is not yet supported for traffic sent to Purview. Scan with Purview only applies to traffic associated with an Entra user identity.
